B. Is this measure already running in Kainuu wellbeing services county (or in the OYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Fitness assessment and prehabilitation before deciding against curative treatment. Before a stage I-III patient is judged too frail, they get an exercise test, a geriatric assessment if over 75, and four weeks of supervised exercise, breathing training and help to stop smoking. Then the decision is made again.
effect_summary_en: A 2022 Cochrane review found that exercise before surgery cut lung complications after surgery (RR 0.45), but it did not measure how many more patients became fit for curative treatment.
supported_en: In a 2022 Cochrane review (10 trials, 636 patients), exercise before lung cancer surgery cut lung complications after surgery (RR 0.45) and shortened hospital stays by about 2.2 days.
not_supported_en: No page measures how much prehabilitation raises the share of patients given curative-intent treatment, so the assumed 0.5 points is not tested.
summary_en: OYS's lung cancer care-pathway page says that the university hospital holds the team meetings and gives surgery and radiotherapy, and that lung function and other illnesses can rule surgery out, but it shows no prehabilitation or re-assessment step; no public sign of it was found for Kainuu or OYS. A 2022 Cochrane review shows that exercise before surgery reduces lung complications afterwards (RR 0.45), but not that more patients become fit for curative treatment.
unanswered_en: Searches of the Kainuu county and OYS sites found no page on prehabilitation or exercise testing before lung cancer surgery, and no study measures the gain in the share of patients treated with curative intent.
